currentContext.expansion: The routed sections disclose no new capex programme, expansion project, commissioning timeline or capacity addition for FY 2025-26. The Directors' Report refers only backward-looking to existing assets: it states that the optimum utilisation of expanded capacities resulted in increased revenue, that the processing (dyeing) unit is fully utilised for dyeing the spinning unit's material with additional material processed in outside dyeing units, and that the Company's windmills are fully utilised for captive consumption by the yarn and processing divisions, with the wind farm generating 333.17 lakh kWh against 282.19 lakh kWh in the previous year and meeting about 90% of total power requirement. No fresh issue of shares was made during the year and no equity shares with differential rights were issued. The only forward-looking operational intent is generic: implementing cost saving measures and expanding market presence in domestic and international markets for value-added yarns. At industry level the MD&A notes that companies investing in capacity expansion, technology upgradation, ESG compliance and product innovation will be well placed, but the Company does not state any such investment of its own.

risks.risk: Cotton price volatility and constrained availability of high-quality cotton
risks.note: The Outlook section names cotton price volatility, changing weather patterns adversely affecting cotton crop yields and constraints on availability of high-quality cotton as the uncertainties management monitors. The MD&A records domestic cotton prices rising from Rs 55,000 per candy in December 2025 to Rs 62,000 per candy by March 2026 even as arrivals increased to 281 lakh bales, which the report says reinforces the importance of disciplined procurement and inventory management. As a spinner, cotton is the dominant input cost.

risks.risk: Overdependence on cotton as raw material, with synthetic fibres under-utilised
risks.note: Listed as a weakness: a heavy focus on cotton makes the business vulnerable to price fluctuations while synthetic fibres remain under-utilised. Separately the MD&A flags that synthetic yarns depend on crude oil derivatives (PTA, MEG) whose prices are unpredictable, and that fluctuations affect working capital and pricing strategy - so both fibre routes carry input-price exposure.

The Company states it operates in only one segment (yarn), and its positioning rests on being a major supplier of melange yarn to the Tirupur market with local presence. There is no diversification cushion if yarn demand or the Tirupur knitwear cluster weakens, and FY 2025-26 already saw yarn production fall to 54.58 lakh kgs from 60.86 lakh kgs and yarn sale volume fall 14.08% to 57.41 lakh kgs.

risks.risk: Fragmented, intensely competitive market limiting pricing power
risks.note: Cited both as a weakness (intense competition in a fragmented market limits pricing power and margin protection) and as a threat (heightened rivalry and aggressive pricing strategies can erode margins and threaten market share). The Company's own stated mitigation is a policy of passing cost increases through on the strength of premium quality, which depends on that pricing power holding.

risks.risk: High capital expenditure intensity constraining financial flexibility
risks.note: Listed as a weakness: significant investment requirements constrain financial flexibility and scalability. The MD&A also observes that companies investing in capacity expansion and technology upgradation will capture a disproportionate share of industry growth, framing under-investment as a competitive risk in a capital-hungry sector.

risks.risk: Environmental footprint of dyeing and spinning, and rising compliance cost
risks.note: The Company runs its own processing (dyeing) unit. The MD&A states that traditional dyeing processes are water-intensive and generate effluents, that energy consumption in spinning and heating processes adds to the carbon footprint, and that the growing need for compliance with environmental regulations adds cost and complexity. It separately flags environmental and reputational scrutiny of synthetic fibre's ecological impact as a threat.

risks.risk: Export competitiveness, tariffs and trade/logistics disruption
risks.note: The industry is described as facing high production costs, complex export procedures and fragmented supply chains that weigh on competitiveness against Vietnam, Bangladesh and China. FY 2025-26 saw trade-route disruption from the US-Iran conflict with shipment delays and a sharp escalation in logistics and shipping costs, while broad US tariff measures from April 2025 created supply-chain uncertainty. The Company's own cotton yarn exports fell 49.60% to 1.29 lakh kgs from 2.56 lakh kgs.

risks.risk: Dependence on government textile policy support and an evolving compliance landscape
risks.note: Management states it expects the Government to support the spinning industry through favourable textile policies, incentives and other benefits, which are described as of paramount importance for the industry's future growth - an explicit dependence on external policy. The MD&A separately lists an evolving regulatory and compliance landscape, where policy shifts and tightening requirements could disrupt operations and increase cost burdens, as a threat.

risks.risk: Demand sensitivity to fashion trends and economic cycles
risks.note: Flagged as a threat: shifts in fashion trends and economic cycles can affect demand consistency and revenue predictability. The Outlook adds global economic uncertainty and evolving tariff conditions as factors introducing unpredictability into the operating environment.
